# Results — Study 61 (Slow-Burn): leveraged-ETF decay, TQQQ vs QQQ, 2010–2026

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Daily total returns of **TQQQ** (3× Nasdaq-
100) and **QQQ** (1×), Yahoo, 2010–2026. Inputs fingerprint `a35f4f6cebe4`.*

## The verdict, earned — Signal `REAL` · Tradability `MIRAGE` · "Leverage is a free return amplifier"? `BUSTED`

The volatility drag is `REAL` and matches theory: a 3× daily-rebalanced QQQ realizes **~8–13%/yr below**
3×(QQQ's CAGR), squarely in line with the textbook **0.5·L·(L−1)·σ² ≈ 12.8%/yr**. But the popular framing
cuts both ways. "Leveraged ETFs always decay to zero" is overstated — in the 2010s bull TQQQ turned QQQ's
**+19.8%/yr into +43.7%/yr**. The honest verdict is `MIRAGE`/`BUSTED`: that bigger number bought **no
risk-adjusted benefit** (Sharpe **0.90 vs QQQ's 0.98**), an **−82% drawdown**, and **−79% in 2022 alone**.
Leverage didn't amplify *returns per unit of risk* at all — it amplified the volatility and the tail, and
quietly bled the drag. A bull-regime bet, not a free multiplier.

## Data stamp

- **Pair**: TQQQ (3×) vs QQQ (1×), daily total return, 2010–2026, 4,107 days, fingerprint `a35f4f6cebe4`

## More return, no more Sharpe — and a catastrophic tail

| | CAGR | Sharpe | vol | max-DD |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QQQ (1×) | +19.8% | **0.98** | 21% | −35% |
| TQQQ (3×) | +43.7% | **0.90** | 61% | **−82%** |

The eye-catching +44%/yr came at triple the volatility, a −82% drawdown, and a *lower* Sharpe than just
owning QQQ. On the only metric that controls for risk, leverage made things slightly worse — and added a
tail that wiped out four-fifths of the position at the trough.

## The volatility drag is real — and matches the formula

| | value |
|---|---|
| naive 3×(QQQ CAGR) | +59.3% |
| 3×-daily-rebalanced, realized | +50.9% |
| **volatility decay (gap)** | **+8.4%/yr** |
| theory: 0.5·L·(L−1)·σ² | **12.8%/yr** |

A daily-rebalanced 3× book compounds at ~8 pts/yr below 3× the underlying's CAGR — the volatility drag,
in line with theory (the realized gap runs a touch under the formula because the strong drift partially
offsets it). The *actual* TQQQ (+43.7%) trails even the self-replicated 3× (+50.9%) by another ~7 pts,
which is fees, financing and tracking. The drag is not a myth; it's arithmetic.

## …but "decays to zero" is the wrong lesson

| TQQQ by regime | CAGR |
|---|---|
| 2010–2021 (bull) | **+55.7%** |
| 2022 (bear) | **−79.2%** |
| 2022–on | +15.8% |

Leverage *amplifies the path*: in a sustained uptrend the daily reset compounds gains spectacularly; in a
choppy or falling market the same reset and the drag destroy capital. TQQQ didn't drift to zero — it 50×'d
in the bull and then lost 79% in one bad year. The danger isn't slow decay; it's that you're holding a
regime bet with ruinous tails and no Sharpe edge.

## The honest takeaway

The volatility drag of leveraged ETFs is `REAL` and matches `0.5·L·(L−1)·σ²` (~13%/yr for 3× QQQ). But
the verdict on *holding* them is `MIRAGE`/`BUSTED`: leverage delivered a bigger return number with **no
risk-adjusted benefit** (Sharpe 0.90 < 0.98), an −82% drawdown and a −79% year. "They always decay to
zero" is too glib — they're a path-dependent, bull-regime bet — but "free return amplifier" is the real
myth.
